name: ReadValues

description: The figures a parsed document stated, taken from the places you say its kind keeps them, with no model, and refused whole when they do not add up to what the document says about itself
whenToUse: Turn a document that was already parsed into figures that can be summed, ranked and compared across many documents: one row per figure, each with what was counted, how it was sliced, its unit, the date it speaks as of, and the sheet and row it came from. It reads what the parse kept, never the file again, because a parse keeps what a document PRINTS and settles a sheet's columns into one grid. It knows no document type of its own: you supply the layouts. Every layout says what must be true of its own reading, and a document whose reading cannot prove itself comes back marked so, with nothing to store.

package.name: documents
package.packageFile:
# DOCUMENTS — the platform's own document service (services/documents, a Python service beside
# umap): a file in, its structure out. Text in reading order, every table as rows, every figure
# as an image with its caption, every ordered list, the dates a document carries, and where on
# which page each sits. docs/unoverse/data/documents/README.md.
#
# ONE DOOR, ONE NODE: ParseDocument, RenderDocument, InventoryFolder, ReadCover, ReadValues. Each is a JOB on
# the service (start, poll, collect), which is the LlamaParse shape, so the poll capability does
# the waiting. A door does one job, so one can be improved or replaced without touching what
# calls it: a census before reading, a cover before filing, a parse when the whole is wanted.
#
# THE HOST IS THE ENGINE, at loopback (`scope.engineUrl`, :4101), which forwards to the service
# (routes/documents.ts) the way it reaches umap. A node's call must be https or loopback
# (allowedHosts.ts refuses a plaintext request to any other host), and a compose service on the
# Docker network is neither; the engine holds the service's address so no node and no file does.

name: documents
displayName: Documents
description: >-
  Read a file into its structure with the platform's document service. Text, tables as rows,
  figures, lists, dates, provenance
version: 0.1.0
category: ingest
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Parse PDF, Word, slides, spreadsheets, HTML and images into one typed structure
  - Tables as rows with units parsed, figures as images, ordered lists as steps
  - Render any page or region as an image
  - "Inventory a folder: kinds, pages, dates, duplicates"
  - "Read a cover: what each file is about and the date it states, from named cells, no model"
  - "Read values: the figures a parsed document stated, refused whole when they do not add up to what it says about itself"

allowedHosts:
  # LOOPBACK ONLY, numeric form (the pattern rejects a bare "localhost"): every call goes to the
  # engine's own listener, which forwards to the service. No third-party host, ever.
  - 127.0.0.1

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  transport: [json]
  # Every door is a job: without `poll` an executor would settle on the receipt and emit the job
  # id as the answer.
  poll: true

files.api/events.yaml:
# A READING THAT CANNOT PROVE ITSELF IS NOT OFFERED. `readings` carries only what came from a
# document whose own checks held, so a caller cannot store unproven figures by forgetting to
# look. What failed is in `unproven`, named, so it can be shown to a person instead.
- emit: readings
  value: >-
    return ((response.result || {}).documents || []).filter(d => d && d.ok).flatMap(d => d.readings || [])

# WHAT WE NEVER LOOKED AT travels with the document (`coverage`). A table no layout names and a
# table with nothing in it are the same absence downstream, and without this a layout that
# quietly loses one of a document's ten tables reads the other nine perfectly and says nothing.
- emit: documents
  value: >-
    return ((response.result || {}).documents || []).map(d => ({ file_name: d.file_name, template: d.template, layout: d.layout || null, subject: d.subject || null, period: d.period || null, found_in: d.found_in || null, ok: d.ok, unproven: d.unproven || [], readings: (d.readings || []).length, coverage: d.coverage || null, error: d.error || null }))

- emit: unproven
  value: >-
    return ((response.result || {}).documents || []).filter(d => d && !d.ok).map(d => ({ file_name: d.file_name, template: d.template, unproven: d.unproven || [], error: d.error || null }))

- emit: total
  value: >-
    return ((response.result || {}).documents || []).filter(d => d && d.ok).reduce((n, d) => n + ((d.readings || []).length), 0)
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [documents, templates]
  properties:
    documents:
      type: string
      title: Documents
      description: >-
        The parsed documents as a JSON array of { file_name, subject, period, tables } or, where
        you hold their addresses rather than their contents, { ..., table_urls }. Usually wired
        from a read, e.g. return signal.documents
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    templates:
      type: string
      title: Layouts
      description: >-
        The layouts you know, as a JSON array. Each is { name, match, observations, checks }:
        `match` is text appearing in every document of that layout and no other; `observations`
        says which sheets, which columns hold which measure and in what unit; `checks` names what
        must be true of the reading afterwards.
      default: "[]"
      "ui:field": template
"ui:order": [documents, templates]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: documents
    type: array
    description: >-
      Each parsed document: { file_name, tables, text }, as the parse kept them. Add `subject` and
      `period` to say what it is about and when it speaks as of; leave them out and they are read
      from the places its layout names
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: readings
    type: array
    description: Every figure read, from the documents whose reading proved itself. One row per figure
  - name: documents
    type: array
    description: >-
      One per document: the layout recognised and that layout whole, what the document says it is
      about and the date it speaks as of with where each was read, ok, unproven, how many readings,
      coverage (how many numbered cells the document held, how many became readings, and the
      tables no block of the layout named), error
  - name: unproven
    type: array
    description: The documents whose reading did not prove itself against what they state about themselves. Their figures are NOT in `readings`
  - name: total
    type: number
    description: How many readings are in `readings`

credentials: []
files.node.yaml:
type: ReadValues
kind: PromiseNode

name: Read Values
category: Documents
color: "#0F766E"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

description: >-
  The figures a parsed document stated, taken from the places you say its kind keeps them, with
  no model, and refused whole when they do not add up to what the document says about itself

whenToUse: >-
  Turn a document that was already parsed into figures that can be summed, ranked and compared
  across many documents: one row per figure, each with what was counted, how it was sliced, its
  unit, the date it speaks as of, and the sheet and row it came from. Use it where the kind of
  document has a fixed layout, so the same file always answers the same way. It reads what the
  parse kept, never the file again, because a parse keeps what a document PRINTS and settles a
  sheet's columns into one grid. It knows no document type of its own: you supply the layouts.
  Every layout says what must be true of its own reading, and a document whose reading cannot
  prove itself comes back marked so, with nothing to store.

auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # REMEMBERED UNDER THE DOCUMENTS SERVICE'S OWN VERSION. This node's answer is decided by that
  # service's code, not by this definition, so a fix to it must forget every answer it gave
  # (2026-09-20: a figures reader was fixed, the service restarted, and the old answer was still
  # served from a trace, silently).
  cacheable:
    answeredBy: documents
files.test.yaml:
# THE NODE UNDER GUARD, against the real service. Two documents of one layout: one whose reading
# proves itself and one whose does not. What matters is that the second's figures never reach
# `readings`, because a reading nobody can check is the one thing this must not hand on quietly.
#
# No document type is named: the layout is the test's own.
testData:
  config:
    documents: >-
      [{"file_name":"good.xlsx","subject":"Example Entity","period":"2026-05-31","tables":[
         {"caption":"2. Exposure","rows":[
           ["2.2","Percentage of Portfolio","","","10","-4","","","",""],
           ["2.4 Sectors","","","","","","","","",""],
           ["","Alpha","","","6","-1","","","",""],
           ["","Beta","","","4","-3","","","",""]]}]},
       {"file_name":"broken.xlsx","subject":"Example Entity","period":"2026-05-31","tables":[
         {"caption":"2. Exposure","rows":[
           ["2.2","Percentage of Portfolio","","","10","-4","","","",""],
           ["2.4 Sectors","","","","","","","","",""],
           ["","Alpha","","","1","-1","","","",""]]}]}]
    templates: >-
      [{"name":"example-layout","match":"Percentage of Portfolio",
        "observations":[{"sheets":["2. Exposure"],"labelColumns":[1,2,3],
          "measures":[{"measure":"exposure","unit":"percent_of_aum","sides":{"long":4,"short":5}}]}],
        "checks":["eachSlicingTotalsWhatTheSheetStates"]}]
  inputs:
    documents: []
  expect:
    readings: "return output.readings.length === 4 && output.readings.every(r => r.measure === 'exposure' && r.unit === 'percent_of_aum' && typeof r.source === 'string')"
    documents: "return output.documents.length === 2 && output.documents[0].ok === true && output.documents[1].ok === false"
    unproven: "return output.unproven.length === 1 && output.unproven[0].file_name === 'broken.xlsx'"
    total: "return output.total === 4"
